questions.question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The energy of light is** inversely proportional** to its wavelength.
 
• Therefore, the light with the **longest wavelength,** i.e. **red**, has the **least energy.**
 
• The colours of VIBGYOR are arranged in **increasing order** of their** wavelengths.**
 
• Hence, **violet** has the** highest energy **and red has the least.
 
• **Green** is the colour of light with a wavelength between yellow and blue.
 
• It has **more energy** than yellow but less than blue.
 
• **Yellow** is the colour of light with a wavelength between green and orange.
 
• It has** less energy** than green but more than orange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **VIBGYOR** stands for** Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red.**

 
 
• These are the** seven colours **of the visible spectrum of light.
 
 
 
• Violet has the **shortest wavelength** and the highest energy among the colours of VIBGYOR.
 
• **Indigo** is a colour that lies between **blue and violet **in the spectrum.
 
 
• It is not always distinguishable from blue and is **not** considered a separate colour by some people.
 
 
 
• **Orange** is a colour that lies between **yellow and red** in the spectrum.
 
 
• It has **more energy** than red but less than yellow.

questions.question: Infrared optical ______ can be used for measuring and monitoring temperatures and hot spots of jet engine rotor blades.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Pyrometer.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• A pyrometer__ is a sort of remote-sensing thermometer that measures the temperature of things that are far away.
 
• Pyrometers have appeared in many forms throughout history.
 
• It can be used for measuring and monitoring temperatures and hot spots of jet engine rotor blades.
 
• It is a device that determines the temperature of a surface from a distance based on the quantity of thermal radiation it produces, a process known as pyrometry and sometimes radiometry.
 
• The majority of pyrometers work by detecting radiation from the body being measured.
 
• It is founded on the idea that the intensity of light received by the observer is proportional to the distance between the observer and the distant source's temperature.
 
• A modern pyrometer consists of an optical system and a detector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• A hygrometer is a device that measures the amount of water vapour present in the air, soil, or restricted places.
 
• An ammeter is a device that measures the current flowing through a circuit.
 
• A Machmeter is a flight instrument in an aircraft's pitot-static system that displays the ratio of true airspeed to sound speed, a dimensionless quantity known as Mach number.

questions.question: If the uncertainty in position and momentum are equal, the uncertainty in velocity will be:
In which among the following orbits does the satellites circle Earth directly above the equator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geostationary orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The satellites that circle Earth directly above the equator are in a Geostationary orbit.
 
• **Geostationary Orbit:**
 
 
• **​**This is a type of geosynchronous orbit, which means the satellite's orbital period is the same as the rotation period of the Earth.
 
 
 
• A satellite in a** Geostationary orbit appears stationary with respect to an observer on the Earth's surface.**
 
• **Location:**
 
 
• **​**Geostationary orbits are directly above the Earth's equator and follow the direction of the Earth's rotation.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **​**These orbits are particularly useful for communication, weather observation, and other satellites that need a constant view of one area of the surface.
 
 
 
• **Orbit Height:**
 
 
• **​**The geostationary orbit is at an altitude of approximately** 35,786 kilometers (22,236 miles) above Earth's equator.**
 
 
 
• **Satellite Speed:**
 
 
• **​**Satellites in geostationary orbit travel at the same rotational speed as the Earth, which allows them to stay in the same position relative to the Earth's surface.

questions.question: The lifting of an object up and down, the parade of an army and the free fall of a heavy object are all examples of which motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rectilinear motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rectilinear motion **is also known as **Linear motion**.
 
• **Rectilinear motion **is **one-dimensional **motion along **a straight line**, and can therefore be described mathematically using **only one spatial dimension**.
 
• A **linear motion **in which the **direction **of the **velocity remains constant **and the **path is a straight line**.
 
• **Gravitational forces **acting on **objects resulting **in **free fall **is an **example **of rectilinear motion.
 
• **Kids sliding down from a slide is **a rectilinear motion.
 
• The motion of **planes in the sky **is a rectilinear motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic motion **is a motion **repeated in equal intervals of time**.
 
• Periodic motion is performed, for example, **by a rocking chair**, a **bouncing ball**, a **vibrating tuning fork**, a **swing in motion**, the **Earth **in its **orbit around the Sun**, and **a water wave**.
 
• **Rotational motion **can be defined as the **motion of an object **around a **circular path**, in a **fixed orbit**.
 
• A **motion repeating itself **is referred to as **periodic or oscillatory motion**.
 
• An **object in **such motion **oscillates **about an **equilibrium position **due to a **restoring force **or **torque**.

questions.question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum wavelength?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **White light **is **split **into** seven colors** when passing through a triangular prism.
 
• The colors that are visible to the human eye are **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue**, **Indigo**, and **Violet**.
 
 
• These colors are commonly remembered using the acronym VIBGYOR.
 
• Typically, the human eye can detect **wavelengths from 380 to 700 nanometers**.
 
 
 
• **Violet **has the **minimum wavelength** among all, and it **deflects the most** when passed through a prism.
 
 
• Shorter wavelengths correspond to higher frequencies and higher energy in the visible spectrum.
 
 
 
• The** wavelength of the colour components** of white light:
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 **Colour**
 **Wavelength (in nanometers (nm))**
 
 

 Violet
 380-450
 
 

 Indigo
 450-480
 
 

 Blue
 480-500
 
 

 Green
 500-570
 
 

 Yellow
 570-590

 590-620
 
 

 Red
 620-750
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the 1660s, English physicist and mathematician Isaac Newton began a series of** experiments with sunlight and prisms**.

 
 
• He demonstrated that clear white light was composed of seven visible colors.
 
• One of the greatest scientific books ever written, Opticks, details Newton's findings from his experiments using prisms to bend light.
 
 
 
• The phenomenon of splitting light into its constituent colors is called dispersion.​
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as refraction.
 
 
• The bending caused by refraction allows us to create rainbows, prisms, magnifying glasses, and lenses.
 
• Our eyes are dependent on this light bending as well.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of sound is measured in hertz (Hz)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequency of the sound.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frequency of the sound characteristics of sound is measured in hertz (Hz). **

 
 
• When sound travels **through air, the atmospheric pressure varies periodically**.

 
 
• The number of pressure variations** per second **is called the frequency of sound,
 
 
 
• Sound wave frequencies can be measured with **a frequency counter or with a spectrum analyzer.**
 
• These devices work by using a microphone to convert the sound wave into an electrical signal.
 
• **The peaks and valleys of the wave** are counted to find the frequency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The intensity of the sound :**

 
 
• Sound intensity, also known** as acoustic intensity**, is defined as** the power carried by sound waves per unit area in a direction perpendicular to that area**.
 
• The SI unit of intensity, which includes **sound intensity, is the watt per square meter (W/m²)**.
 
• Sound intensity is not the same physical quantity as sound pressure.
 
 
 
• **The loudness of the sound :**
 
 
• Loudness refers to how **loud or soft a sound seems to a listener.**
 
• The loudness of sound is determined, in turn, by the intensity of the sound waves.
 
• Intensity is a measure of the amount of energy in sound waves.
 
• The unit of intensity is the** decibel (dB).**
 
 
 
• **The wavelength of the sound :**
 
 
• The wavelength of a sound, therefore, is t**he distance between adjacent identical parts of a sound wave.**
 
• Just as** the distance between adjacent crests in a transverse wave is one wavelength.**
 
• the distance between adjacent compressions in a sound wave is also one wavelength,

questions.question: Which experiment was designed to trace the motion of the earth through the 'luminiferous aether', a theoretical substance necessary for the transmission of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Michelson and Morley experiment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Michelson and Morley experiment was designed to trace the earth's motion through the luminiferous aether, a theoretical substance necessary for transmitting light.**
 
• The experiment was conducted in **1887 by Albert Michelson and Edward Morley.**
 
• The experiment aimed to detect the relative motion of the earth and the luminiferous aether by measuring the speed of light in different directions.
 
• The experiment results were surprising as they showed that the speed of light was constant in all directions, which contradicted the prevailing theory of the existence of the luminiferous aether.
 
• The Michelson and Morley experiment paved the way for the development of Einstein's theory of relativity, which explained the behavior of light and the absence of the luminiferous aether.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maxwell and Hertz experiment: **This experiment was conducted by James Clerk Maxwell and Heinrich Hertz in the late 19th century to demonstrate the existence of electromagnetic waves.
 
• **Faraday and Henry experiment:** This experiment was conducted by Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry in the 19th century to study the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction.
 
• **Marconi and Thomson experiment: **This experiment was conducted by Guglielmo Marconi and Joseph John Thomson in the early 20th century to demonstrate the feasibility of wireless communication.

questions.question: The potential difference, V, across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. This is called ______ law.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Ohm's**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The relationship between current, voltage, and resistance is described by Ohm's law. This law is given by George Simon Ohm in 1828

Ohm’s law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law states that at a constant temperature, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• Voltage = Current × Resistance
 
 
• V = I × R
 
• V = voltage, I = current and R = resistance
 
 
 
• The SI unit of resistance is ohms and is denoted by Ω.
 
• It helps to calculate the power, efficiency, current, voltage, and resistance of an element of an electrical circuit.
 
• If an element follows ohm’s law, then the element is known as a linear element.
 
• Ex: Resistor

Limitation of ohm's Law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law is applicable for conductors only.
 
• Ohm’s law does not apply to unilateral networks. Unilateral networks allow the current to flow in one direction. Such types of networks consist of elements like a diode, transistor, etc.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to non - linear elements.
 
• Non-linear elements are those which do not have current exactly proportional to the applied voltage that means the resistance value of those elements changes for different values of voltage and current. An example of a non-linear element is a thyristor.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to vacuum tubes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Boyle’s Law**

 
• ​Boyle's law is a gas law that states that a gas's pressure and volume are inversely proportional.
 
• It states that at a constant temperature, the pressure exerted by a gas is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by it.
 
• According to the Boyle's Law:
 
 
• P1V1 = P2V2
 
 
• Where P1 = Initial Pressure

 P2 = Final Pressure

 V1 = Initial Volume 

 V2 = Final Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/883ca4a9c62fe7d942ab5573518c8cee4603dd50fc0953b220b928a0f514f177.png] 
 
 
 
 

The five main gas laws in chemistry are Boyle's Law, Charle's Law, Gay Lussac's Law, Avogadro's Law, and Ideal Gas Law.

 
• Charle's law states that the volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature at constant pressure.
 
• Gay-Lussac's law states that the pressure of a given mass of gas varies directly with the absolute temperature of the gas when the volume is kept constant.
 
• Avogadro's law or Avogadro-Ampère's hypothesis is an experimental gas law relating the volume of a gas to the amount of substance of gas present.
 
• The ideal gas law states that the product of the pressure and the volume of one gram molecule of an ideal gas is equal to the product of the absolute temperature of the gas and the universal gas constant.

questions.question: The earthquake waves are recorded by an instrument called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seismograph**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A seismograph is an instrument **used to detect and record earthquakes.**
 
• The first seismograph was developed in 1890.
 
 
• It consists of a mass attached to a fixed base and during an earthquake, the base moves and the mass does not.
 
• The motion of the base with respect to the mass is commonly transformed into an **electrical voltage.**
 
• The electrical voltage is recorded on **paper, magnetic tape, or another recording medium.**
 
• This record is proportional to the motion of the seismometer mass relative to the earth, but it can be mathematically converted to a record of the absolute motion of the ground. ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67ab952367d3b0c492db0bdd199d8e0b5c72695a16891b478a64d90a122fcd3b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earthquake**: 

 
 
• Earthquakes are caused by **seismic waves that are generated due to a sudden movement in the earth's crust. **
 
• Earthquakes may occur naturally or as a result of human activities.
 
• Tectonic earthquakes are generated due to the sliding of rocks along a fault plane. 
 
• Volcanic earthquakes are caused due to violent volcanic eruptions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Heat, in ______, is a type of energy transfer from a warmer substance to a colder one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**thermodynamics.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Heat is the form of energy that is transferred between two substances at different temperatures.
 
• The direction of energy flow is from the substance of higher temperature to the substance of lower temperature.
 
• Heat is measured in units of energy, usually **calories **or **joules**.
 
• **Thermodynamics **is the** study of the relations between heat, work, temperature, and energy. **
 
• The laws of thermodynamics describe how the energy in a system changes and whether the system can perform useful work on its surroundings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnet **- A magnet is a material or object that produces a magnetic field that pulls on other ferromagnetic materials, such as iron, steel, nickel, cobalt, etc.
 
• **Friction **is a force between two surfaces that are sliding, or trying to slide, across each other.
 
• **Gravity** is the force by which a planet or other body draws objects toward its center. The force of gravity keeps all of the planets in orbit around the sun.

questions.question: What is the wavelength range of visible light ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.4 to 0.7 µm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The wavelength range of **visible light** is typically from **0.4 to 0.7 µm** (micrometers).
 
• This range corresponds to the colors violet (at the shortest wavelength) to red (at the longest wavelength) within the visible spectrum.
 
• Visible light is the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum that is detectable by the human eye.
 
• Wavelengths shorter than 0.4 µm fall into the ultraviolet range, while wavelengths longer than 0.7 µm fall into the infrared range.
 
• Understanding the wavelength range of visible light is crucial in fields such as optics, photography, and astronomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton** was one of the first scientists to study the properties of light and to demonstrate that white light could be split into its component colors using a prism.
 
• The study of light and its interactions is known as **optics**, a branch of physics.
 
• The visible spectrum is just a small part of the entire electromagnetic spectrum, which includes other types of waves such as radio waves, microwaves, X-rays, and gamma rays.
 
• Technological applications that utilize the visible light spectrum include **LED lighting, fiber optics, and lasers**.
 
• The concept of wavelength is essential in understanding phenomena such as diffraction, interference, and the Doppler effect.

questions.question: Which device is used to measure the current flow using needle deflection caused by a magnetic field force acting upon a current - carrying wire?

__
 
• A **Galvanometer** is an instrument for detecting and measuring electric current by needle deflection.
 
• The deflection is caused by a magnetic field force acting upon a current-carrying wire within the device.
 
• It is a type of sensitive ammeter and can measure small currents accurately.
 
• Galvanometers are widely used in various applications including in analog meters and in the calibration of other instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It operates on the principle of electromagnetism, where an electric current creates a magnetic field.
 
• There are different types of galvanometers, including the moving coil and moving magnet types.
 
• Modern digital multimeters have largely replaced galvanometers for many applications but they are still used in specific scientific experiments and educational settings.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT applicable to force?

options.text: Force may make an object move
Force may change the direction of a moving object
Force may change the shape of an object
Force may increase the mass of the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Force may increase the mass of the object**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Force may make an object move:** When a force is applied to an object, it can cause the object to start moving if it was initially at rest.
 
• **Force may change the direction of a moving object:** Forces can alter the trajectory of an object in motion, such as a ball being hit in a different direction.
 
• **Force may change the shape of an object:** Applying force can deform objects, such as squeezing a rubber ball.
 
• **Force may increase the mass of the object:** This statement is incorrect. Force cannot change the mass of an object; mass is an intrinsic property of matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force** is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Newton's second law of motion states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of that object times its acceleration (F = ma).

 
• Forces can be contact forces (e.g., friction, tension) or non-contact forces (e.g., gravity, electromagnetic forces).

 
• Understanding the effects of forces is fundamental in fields such as physics, engineering, and mechanics.

questions.question: Who proposed that ‘Light is made up of waves propagating perpendicular to the direction of its movement’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Huygens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Christiaan Huygens** was a Dutch physicist, mathematician, astronomer and inventor.
 
• He is best known for his wave theory of light, which he described in his book **"Traité de la Lumière"** (Treatise on Light) in 1690.
 
• Huygens proposed that **light is made up of waves** that propagate perpendicular to the direction of its movement.
 
• This wave theory of light was later supported by the experiments of **Thomas Young** and **Augustin-Jean Fresnel**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wave Theory of Light:**

 
 
• The wave theory of light suggests that light travels in the form of waves.
 
• According to Huygens' principle, every point on a wavefront is a source of wavelets that spread out in the forward direction at the same speed as the wave itself.
 
• The new wavefront is the tangent to all of these secondary wavelets.
 
• This theory was instrumental in explaining phenomena such as interference and diffraction, which could not be explained by the particle theory of light.
 
 
 
• **Particle Theory of Light:**
 
 
• The particle theory of light, proposed by Isaac Newton, suggested that light is made up of particles called corpuscles.
 
• This theory was successful in explaining the reflection and refraction of light but failed to explain interference and diffraction.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Young's Double-Slit Experiment:**
 
 
• Thomas Young's double-slit experiment demonstrated the wave nature of light.
 
• When light passes through two closely spaced slits, it creates an interference pattern on a screen behind the slits.
 
• This pattern of bright and dark fringes can only be explained if light behaves as a wave.
 
 
 
• **Augustin-Jean Fresnel:**
 
 
• Fresnel made significant contributions to the wave theory of light.
 
• He developed the Fresnel equations, which describe how light behaves at the interface between two different media.
 
• Fresnel's work on diffraction and interference further confirmed the wave nature of light.
